newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products see growing jet fuel demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products see growing jet fuel demand.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed with fuel oil steady and light distillates continuing its slide, while jet fuel prices continued to rise as regional demand improves, traders said.

Traders said China has bought a total of 100,000 tonnes jet fuel from three traders over the past week for delivery during the fourth quarter. The price ranged between $1.95 and $2.10 a barrel over Singapore quotes c+f northeast China. Demand also emerged from Taiwan that has issued a tender to buy 32,000 tonnes of Oct 10-20 delivery jet fuel, which closes September 4. Japan's winter demand has also not yet been covered.

Indonesia's September jet fuel demand hovered around 1.5 million barrels, because of a CDU shutdown at the Cilacap refinery in September and at Balongan in October. Most of its September demand has been covered, traders said. A major raised its bid for 120,000 barrels to $28.90 for September 21-25, 10 cents over Tuesday. An offer was seen for September 12-16 at $29.10, fob. Bullish traders said unlike last year, the closed jet fuel arbitrage from the US Gulf Coast and the Mediterranean because of the strong western middle-distillates market would help the jet fuel market remain strong even if the this year's winter was not as severe as last year.

Gas oil was steady with Indonesia seen taking 3.5 million September barrels. China continued to seek September cargoes around $200 a tonne c+f. A US trader bought 200,000 barrels of gas oil at $25.65 from a European major for September 20-25. Naphtha fell on lower crudes and talk of petrochemical shutdowns in September and October. Taiwan bought two, not one 3,500-tonne MTBE cargo on talk of a Saudi plant shutdown. Gasoline was supported with 50,000 barrels of 92 octane unleaded traded at $20.55 for September 21-25 lifting. Fuel oil was rangebound with China staying away or bidding September 180-cst at very low prices of $108-$109 a tonne. --RAMTHAN HUSSAIN (+65-8703084)
